Orchestrator proxy reconnects caused private control-plane flaps — action items

Summary: During a scheduled minor upgrade to the Private control plane (orchestrator agent and proxy bundle), a subset of customer VPCs experienced transient control-plane disconnects lasting 30-120s. Impact: API calls to private control plane (health checks, model status, deployments) either timed out or were routed to a stale proxy resulting in failed deploys and delayed autoscaling for ~12 customer clusters. Background: The migration introduced a new lightweight proxy handshake intended to reduce connection churn. Under specific NAT and load-balancing configurations, the proxy handshake repeatedly timed out and triggered orchestrator reconnection attempts, which exacerbated state divergence in the control plane cluster membership.
2026-02-25 02:10 UTC - Scheduled upgrade window started.
2026-02-25 02:34 UTC - First spike in control-plane errors observed: increased 502/504 to private endpoints.
2026-02-25 02:37 UTC - Pager triggered (oncall: S. Martinez).
2026-02-25 02:43 UTC - Rollback of proxy change attempted on a canary host.
2026-02-25 03:05 UTC - Partial rollback completed; errors reduced but persisted for customers behind specific NAT gateway setups.
2026-02-25 04:00 UTC - Hotfix deployed that increased proxy handshake timeout and fallback to TCP keepalive; incidents subsided.
2026-02-25 08:00 UTC - Post-incident war room.
2026-02-26 15:00 UTC - Initial RCA draft shared.
Edge case interaction between short proxy handshake timeout and intermediate NAT/load-balancer idle timeouts. When connections traversed certain managed NAT gateways with aggressive UDP/TCP port reuse and a 30s idle cleanup, the new proxy handshake frequently observed half-closed sockets which caused the orchestrator to consider the proxy dead and reconnect. Rapid reconnects created brief membership churn and a small window where control-plane routing directed traffic to outdated proxy instances.
1) Immediate rollback of the new aggressive proxy keepalive behavior during the incident. 2) Hotfix increased handshake timeout and introduced exponential backoff on reconnects. 3) Temporary control-plane routing grace window added to avoid immediate failover while reconnections settle. 4) Customer comms sent to affected tenants with steps and mitigations. 5) Added monitoring to track proxy handshake latency, reconnection rate, and NAT-specific error patterns.
Owner: Liam O'Connor — Task: Implement configurable handshake timeout per-deployment and default to conservative value for Private. Due: 2026-03-12 — Tickets: ENG-34195
Owner: Priya Shah — Task: Add deterministic exponential backoff to orchestrator reconnection logic (client-side) and circuit-breaker threshold. Due: 2026-03-05 — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/4821
Owner: Network Eng Team (lead: Mateo Rivera) — Task: Create doc mapping known cloud NAT/load-balancer timeouts and recommended VPC settings for Private customers; include detection heuristics in onboarding checks. Due: 2026-03-19 — Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/NET/NAT-Timeouts
Owner: Observability (lead: Sofia Martinez) — Task: Add dashboard and alerting for proxy-handshake-failures, rapid-reconnect-rate, and per-cluster control-plane routing churn. Due: 2026-03-08 — Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/private-proxy/handshake
Owner: Security & Compliance (lead: Elena Park) — Task: Review handshake timeout changes for any TLS or HSM implications and sign off. Due: 2026-03-10

Review follow-ups at weekly reliability sync (2026-03-11). Recommend graduating the temporary routing grace window into a tunable rollout feature that can be enabled in high-risk networks. Consider offering a Private deployment preflight check during install to detect aggressive NATs and suggest configuration adjustments. We need to validate that the conservative defaults do not materially impact latency targets for Dedicated customers.
